page.title: Investor Relations Event Production Guide
page.description: Learn the key decisions, timelines, and production checklist for investor relations events, from format choice to rehearsal proof and backup stream readiness.
page.h1: What should you decide first about investor relations event production?
page.definition: Investor relations event production is the end‑to‑end planning and live execution of earnings calls, analyst days, and shareholder webcasts, covering format selection, platform setup, speaker rehearsal, run‑of‑show ownership, and backup stream readiness. It also includes compliance timing, Q&A moderation, and post‑event replay delivery.
page.quick_answer: Choose the audience outcome and format first, then lock the platform and venue AV before finalising the agenda; West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: Which audience outcome and format should drive the event design?

blocks.p: Start by defining the investor outcome you need, such as earnings transparency, analyst engagement, or shareholder voting, then pick the format that serves that outcome. Align the format with regulatory timing, branding requirements, and the expected Q&A flow.

ul: Select live webcast, hybrid town hall, or on‑demand briefing
Agree on branding and compliance sign‑off

sections.h2: What platform and venue decisions must be locked early?

blocks.p: Lock the streaming platform and any physical venue AV before the agenda is final to avoid last‑minute compatibility gaps. Confirm that the platform supports required compliance features, registration integration, and analytics.

head: Category
Typical Use
rows: Multi‑session summits with registration and analytics

sections.h2: How do you manage late assets and rehearsal proof?

blocks.p: Set a hard asset deadline, run a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and complete a technical check sixty minutes before go‑live. This catches slide timing, audio levels, and backup stream readiness.

ol: Collect slides, videos, and compliance disclosures by the asset deadline
Load all assets into the platform and verify playback
Run full rehearsal with every speaker and moderator
Document any issues and assign fixes
Perform final technical check sixty minutes before start

sections.h2: What staffing model fits a webinar versus a summit?

blocks.p: A simple webinar needs one producer, while a summit or hybrid event requires a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, and platform operator. Hybrid adds an on‑site AV lead and a remote stream engineer.

ul: Webinar: single producer handles run‑of‑show, Q&A, and backup stream
Summit: show caller cues transitions, speaker manager coordinates rehearsals, moderator fields questions, platform operator monitors streams
Hybrid: add on‑site AV lead and remote stream engineer

sections.h2: When should the replay and follow‑up be delivered?

blocks.p: Publish the edited recording and key clips within twenty four to forty eight hours, then push follow‑up emails and CRM updates while the event is still fresh. Early delivery reinforces key messages and supports compliance archiving.

faq.q: How far in advance should the agenda be finalised for a hybrid investor day?
faq.a: Finalise the agenda at least six to eight weeks before the event so venue AV, platform configuration, and speaker briefs can be locked without rush. This timeline also allows compliance review and investor communication scheduling. Early lock prevents last minute changes that risk streaming stability.

faq.q: What is the minimum rehearsal window for a live earnings call?
faq.a: Run a full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the call and a final technical check sixty minutes prior to go live. This window catches slide timing, audio levels, and backup stream readiness. It also gives speakers confidence and reduces on‑air errors consistently.

faq.q: Which roles can be combined for a small‑team webinar?
faq.a: One producer can own run‑of‑show, Q&A moderation, and backup stream monitoring when the event is a single‑session webinar. If compliance sign‑off is required, add a legal reviewer to the same call. This keeps cost low while preserving live quality consistently.

faq.q: What backup plan protects a hybrid investor event from stream failure?
faq.a: Maintain a secondary encoder on a separate internet path, record locally, and assign a platform operator to switch feeds instantly if the primary drops. Test the failover during rehearsal so the switch is seamless. Document the procedure in the run‑of‑show for every crew member.
